about: Thro's decision tree. Each node is a decision held in place by its parent. Active: composed into this site. Open: waiting on a choice; alternatives listed. Subsumed: no longer in the site; kept with the iteration where it was live. Previews: https://iter-N.thro.pages.dev

nodes.question: What matters most on a card?
nodes.choice: DISC IMAGE > MOLD NAME > FLIGHT NUMBERS > everything else. Flight numbers carry no labels: written like a score, 6.5 · 5 · −1 · 2.

nodes.question: Which build do the Single-screen improvements sit on?
nodes.choice: The original thro build (f4667ee).

nodes.question: Which build is thro built on?
nodes.choice: Dab's native-card build (4bd0214), with iterations 1–9 replayed onto it.

nodes.question: How should the preview frame the graphic?
nodes.choice: Close-up by default, Whole frame one tap away.

nodes.question: How do you choose a layout?
nodes.choice: Rendered thumbnails with your disc in them, cached so they never blank.

nodes.question: Where does a download say it worked?
nodes.choice: Right at the button, with the file name.

nodes.question: Where does the accent colour come from?
nodes.choice: Match disc: sampled from the plastic, or a fixed palette.

nodes.question: Can a tap be lost while the graphic redraws?
nodes.choice: No: Download and Keep stay live while it redraws.

nodes.question: What happens when you keep the same version twice?
nodes.choice: It says Already kept; kept graphics show cropped to the graphic.

nodes.question: Does the preview remember how you like to see it?
nodes.choice: Yes: background and framing come back after reload.

nodes.question: Dab's three findings on iter-10
nodes.choice: Framing keeps focus; a failed module can't hang startup; recovery buttons clear the export bar.

nodes.question: How are Single cards composed?
nodes.choice: One renderer: every Single card is a DiscStudio card, composed the same way.

nodes.question: Vector compositions in Single (placement grid, title field)
nodes.choice: Retired from Single; still used by Battle until Battle moves.

nodes.question: How fast is a card, and can the rule be checked?
nodes.choice: Each card draws once (0.7 s → 0.12 s, pixel-identical) and reports where the disc, name and numbers landed.

nodes.question: Can lineups use the same cards?
nodes.choice: Yes: the lab showed 2–4 exact cards in one frame.

nodes.question: What does a Bag lineup look like?
nodes.choice: Each disc is its exact card; no points or UP NOW; one disc can be featured.

nodes.question: How do you adjust a card?
nodes.choice: On the card: drag to move, knob to size; Side, Accent and Plate in a strip under the preview, never on the card.

nodes.question: How does Battle work?
nodes.choice: Its own editor. One model: entries × holes; each format is a class with compare(a, b) → int.
